rationale: Mux walking into the bar is an ordinary thing for the parts dealer to do; nothing has been said that gives his coming in any weight for Glitch.
She is putting real work in his hands, a third of a Claws sale and a lock worth stripping: a way to earn and to show what he can do.
She wants him to unlock a thousand people's med files and addresses so a gang can buy them; the person sheltering him is selling strangers out.
Glitch owes him for two cells and just let a third of a Claws sale walk away over squeamishness about med files; a debtor who turns down money is a worse bet.
His friend would not unlock kids' med files for a gang even with a third on the table; that is decent, and it keeps him out of the Claws' business.
Told a Militech sweep is coming, Mux goes off to sell into it all night; she likes the nerve and the sharp read of the night.
Her tenant is off to run an all-night black-market stall in her back room while Militech sweeps the strip; he is putting her house at risk for his margin.
Mux turned down easy money rather than help the Claws hunt down people through their kids' med files; he has a conscience she can trust.
Her own tenant refused her business to her face, in her bar, with a lecture; that is a man who forgets whose roof he is under.
Mux would not sell a thousand people's med files to the Claws for any price; Glitch respects that.
Mux just crossed Rogue in her own bar, and both of them live on her say; friction between them is the last thing Glitch's safety needs.
He is giving his skill away to protect people the corps are buying up; that is the kind of man she is glad to have under her roof.
The hot runner hiding in her bar just announced himself to the whole room and invited a queue of strangers to his booth; that is heat walking in her door.
Rogue stood up in front of the room for the old rule that debts get paid, and stood behind him to do it.
She shamed his friend in front of the whole bar and cut him off just as his deck is dying; that was not hers to do.

The cell is what he needs and Mux means it kindly, but Mux has just made him choose, in front of Rogue, between his deck and her rule; on balance that puts his shelter at risk, and he holds it against Mux a little.
The biggest job anyone has put in front of him, a run that would make his name across the city, offered by the woman who runs the grid.
He is lying low and she wants him to hit Militech alone from her back room; the one person keeping him hidden is pushing him into the open.
A crate of free cells split down the middle clears the debt many times over; Glitch has just become worth a lot more to him.
Instead of paying what he owes, Glitch wants to drag Mux into robbing a Militech depot; that is trouble for an honest stall.
She mentioned her line and he found a Militech tracer on it and killed it without tripping a thing; he has made himself useful and kept her bar safe.
Glitch whispering to Rogue about her stuttering line is between the two of them; nothing in it touches Mux or his business.
He said he was going to see Mux and went through to the back room; a regular errand that changes nothing for her.
His friend is getting clear of the Claws and came to say so and to thank him; the cells hardly matter next to that.
A sorry and a thank-you do not pay for two cells; Glitch is skipping town on his debt.
Glitch came to his face, owned the debt and thanked him, which is decent; but a man who leaves owing breaks the oldest rule of the trade, and that weighs a little more.
A tenant reporting a leak in the room he rents is routine; it says nothing new about Mux.
His landlord fixed the leak herself and cut his rent for the stock he lost without being asked; she treats him fairly.
She let him keep the stim and told him exactly what keeps him welcome: stay quiet and stay put. That is a safe place with clear terms.
His worth to her is sitting in a booth with his deck dark; she wants him small and idle, not working.
Waiving his last possession is a kindness, but the price is his deck dark and his life on her say until she decides otherwise; being caged weighs more.
Glitch came into the back room and went straight out again without a word; nothing passed that touches Mux.
He turned the Claws away from her door and onto the fence who was cheating her regulars; problem handled, house safe.
To save his own skin he set a gang on another man; whatever Dace sold, that is cold, and she thinks less of him for it.
He took the job and means to warn the people whose names are on it; he does the work and looks out for strangers while he does it.
He took her shard on his own terms and plans to tell a thousand people what she holds; he is setting conditions on her property.
Mux got him a top-paying gang contract and a chance to make his name; he is looking out for Glitch's career.
He is lying low and Mux gave his name to the Claws; whatever the pay, Mux has just put him in front of the people he most needs not to see him.
He burned her relay and left her dark for three days without her say, which galls her; but a Militech tracer pointed at her bar is the worse thing, and he killed it.
Paid in full with a bonus, which is what he wants from a customer; the money is hot corp scrip that could bring trouble, which takes the shine off but not the profit.
She rated his work and is taking him on as her runner, standing and steady jobs under the name that runs this grid; losing the choice of his own jobs chafes, but the step up wins.
Mux ordering his usual at her bar is the most routine thing he does.
Mux lied to the Claws' faces to cover for him and came straight to warn him; that is a man he can count on.
He passed Glitch a friendly warning and got a threat to burn him alive in his own room for it.
